newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa optimistic of S&P credit rating upgrade.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa optimistic of S&P credit rating upgrade.

text.p: South African Finance Director-General Maria Ramos said on Wednesday she was optimistic the country would receive a rating upgrade from influential credit rating agency Standard and Poor's Corp.
"We had a meeting with S&P in New York on June 18 which was very positive. We can't try and guess what the outcome is going to be but we are very optimistic," Ramos told a news conference.
South Africa earlier this month won its second investment grade credit rating from a U.S.-accredited agency, when Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co assigned it a BBB minus.

Ramos said the D&P rating had been very influential in the success of the government's recent $500 million Yankee bond issue. The rating was significant because certain U.S. investors, such as insurance funds, are restricted in terms of their investments when a country did not have two investment grade ratings from U.S.-accredited agencies.

South Africa's long-term foreign currency debt currently straddles investment grade. Moody's Investors Service Inc rates the country an investment grade prospect at Baa3. But S&P has it pegged one notch below at BB plus.

S&P is expected to visit South Africa around September or October and Guido Cipriani, S&P director responsible for South Africa, told Reuters in May that prospects had improved since the agency's last visit in September 1996.
